subject: Made-to-measure alcove cabinetry
hook: Two empty alcoves, one plan: how they become storage.
ig:
Two empty alcoves, one plan: here's how they typically become storage that looks like it was always there.

The fresh-start month is a good time to deal with the corners that collect clutter. This is the principle, step by step:

The empty alcove, with its uneven walls and awkward socket.
The survey, measuring at several heights.
The split: cupboards below for the things you'd rather not see, shelves above for the things you would.
The workshop, where the carcasses are cut, edged and assembled.
The fit, with scribed fillers and socket access kept.
The finish: two alcoves doing a real job.

These frames are concept images showing how the process works. Real SUPERIO furniture is on our showcase. Save this if your alcoves are on this year's list, and see genuine work via the link in bio.
fb:
January is when the clutter really shows. If yours tends to gather in the alcoves either side of the chimney breast, here's how that space typically gets turned into proper storage.

We measure the alcoves at several heights, agree a layout (cupboards below and shelves above is the most popular), make everything in our Hanley workshop, then fit it with filler panels scribed to your walls so there are no gaps.

These are concept images to show the stages. For finished SUPERIO furniture, have a look at our showcase.

alt: Six-frame carousel moving from an empty alcove beside a chimney breast to measured drawings, workshop assembly and finished fitted cupboards with shelves (AI concept images).
on_asset: F1: The empty alcove — Wasted space either side of the chimney breast, often with a socket, uneven walls and a skirting board in the way. | F2: Survey — Width at three heights, depth to the breast, sockets, skirting and floor level all go on the drawing. | F3: The split — A typical layout: closed cupboards below for clutter, open shelves above for books and display. | F4: Workshop — Carcasses cut, edged and assembled in Hanley, quality-checked before they leave. | F5: Fitted — Filler panels scribed to the walls, socket access kept, shelves levelled. | F6: Finished — Two alcoves that now hold the things that used to sit on the floor. | Concept image
